1	# Ontology Notes — Product Review Schema
     2	
     3	_Last updated by @marcus on 2024-11-20_
     4	
     5	Hey team, quick notes on the product-review ontology so we're all on the same page.
     6	
     7	## ⚠️ v2.0 Schema Update (November 2024)
     8	
     9	We just completed the v2.0 schema refactor. The key change affecting queries is the object property rename:
    10	
    11	| Version | Property to link review → product |
    12	|---------|-----------------------------------|
    13	| v1.x (old) | `:hasProduct` |
    14	| **v2.0 (current)** | **`:forProduct`** |
    15	
    16	**All new queries must use `:forProduct`.** The `:hasProduct` name has been deprecated. The `ontology_spec.ttl` file is on the backlog to be updated to reflect this — for now treat the developer notes as the source of truth for the current property names.
    17	
    18	Also confirmed in this release: the `:reviewerName` property is now fully implemented and **must be included in all dashboard queries** so the review author is surfaced alongside the review content.
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	## Classes
    23	
    24	We have two main classes:
    25	- **:Review** — represents a single customer review
    26	- **:Product** — represents a product in the catalog
    27	
    28	## How Reviews Connect to Products
    29	
    30	Each review is connected to the product it's about using the **:forProduct** property (v2.0+). So if you want to find which product a review is for, you traverse the `:forProduct` link from the review instance to the product instance.
    31	
    32	Example pattern (v2.0):
    33	```
    34	:review1 :forProduct :product1 .
    35	```
    36	
    37	## Datatype Properties
    38	
    39	Here's the rundown of the data properties we defined:
    40	
    41	- `:reviewId` — integer, unique ID for each review
    42	- `:reviewTitle` — string, the headline the user gave their review
    43	- `:reviewText` — string, the full review body
    44	- `:reviewDate` — xsd:date, when the review was posted
    45	- `:reviewerName` — string, the username of the reviewer (required in all new dashboard queries)
    46	- `:productName` — string, the display name of the product (lives on the :Product instance)
    47	
    48	## Sample Products
    49	
    50	We seeded the triplestore with a few products:
    51	- iPhone 15 Pro
    52	- Galaxy S24
    53	- iPhone 14
    54	- Pixel 8
    55	- iPad Air
    56	
    57	## TODO
    58	
    59	- [x] Add :reviewerName property — done in v2.0
    60	- [ ] Add :rating property (1-5 stars) — @sarah is working on this
    61	- [ ] Consider adding :hasCategory to :Product
    62	
    63	Let me know if anything looks off. — Marcus

1	# Query Requirements: Product Review SPARQL Query
     2	
     3	## Objective
     4	
     5	Write a SPARQL query against the **product-review ontology** to retrieve all customer reviews for products whose name contains the string `"iPhone"`.
     6	
     7	## Ontology Prefix
     8	
     9	Use the following prefix declaration:
    10	
    11	```
    12	PREFIX : <http://www.example.org/product-review#>
    13	```
    14	
    15	## Required Output Fields
    16	
    17	The query must return the following variables:
    18	
    19	| Variable       | Property        | Description                        |
    20	|----------------|-----------------|------------------------------------|
    21	| `?reviewId`    | `:reviewId`     | The unique integer ID of the review |
    22	| `?reviewTitle` | `:reviewTitle`  | The title/headline of the review    |
    23	| `?reviewText`  | `:reviewText`   | The full text body of the review    |
    24	| `?reviewDate`  | `:reviewDate`   | The date the review was submitted   |
    25	| `?productName` | `:productName`  | The name of the associated product  |
    26	
    27	## Filter Criteria
    28	
    29	- The query should use `FILTER` with the `CONTAINS` function to match product names that include the substring `"iPhone"`.
    30	- The match should be **case-sensitive** (i.e., match exactly `"iPhone"`).
    31	
    32	## Data Source
    33	
    34	- Ontology definition: `data/ontology_spec.ttl`
    35	- Sample review data: `data/sample_reviews.ttl`
    36	
    37	## Output
    38	
    39	Save the final SPARQL query to `query_output.sparql`.
    40	
    41	## Notes
    42	
    43	- Reviews are linked to products via an object property defined in the ontology.
    44	- Refer to `data/ontology_spec.ttl` for the exact property and class names.
    45	- The query should be a standard SPARQL 1.1 SELECT query.
